original_question: Which abelian pro-Lie groups are strongly reflexive, in the sense that every subgroup and every Hausdorff quotient group is reflexive?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Question 4: Which Abelian pro-Lie groups are strongly reflexive in the sense that all of their subgroups and Hausdorff quotient groups are reflexive? ([mdpi.com](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-1680/4/3/294))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's exact target almost verbatim: it has the correct class of groups, the correct property name, and the correct closure requirement under subgroups and Hausdorff quotient groups. ([mdpi.com](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-1680/4/3/294))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, it should define reflexive in the paper's Pontryagin-duality sense: for an Abelian topological group A, A^ = Hom(A,T) with the compact-open topology, T = R/Z, and A is reflexive when the canonical evaluation map η_A: A -> (A^)^ is an isomorphism of topological groups. ([sidneymorris.net](https://www.sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf?utm_source=openai))

It should make explicit that subgroups are taken with their inherited topology; the paper quantifies over all subgroups, not merely closed subgroups. ([mdpi.com](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-1680/4/3/294))
It should keep the paper's restriction to Hausdorff quotient groups, rather than all algebraic quotients without a Hausdorff condition. ([mdpi.com](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-1680/4/3/294))

For paper-faithful context, this question is posed after Theorem 6 decomposes any Abelian pro-Lie group into a weakly-complete vector part and a part with compact connected identity component, and after Theorem 7 proves that every almost connected Abelian pro-Lie group is reflexive; the remaining difficulty is therefore beyond the almost connected case, especially around groups with compact identity component, including prodiscrete groups. ([sidneymorris.net](https://sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Which Abelian pro-Lie groups G are strongly reflexive, meaning that for every subgroup H ≤ G endowed with the inherited topology and every Hausdorff quotient group Q of G, the canonical Pontryagin evaluation map η_A: A -> (A^)^ is an isomorphism of topological groups for A = H and A = Q, where A^ = Hom(A,T) carries the compact-open topology and T = R/Z? ([mdpi.com](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-1680/4/3/294))
justification: The draft is aiming at Section 4, Question 4 exactly, not at a broader neighboring problem. The nearby context first defines semireflexive and reflexive via the evaluation map into the Pontryagin double dual, then discusses a prodiscrete example showing that reflexivity issues are nontrivial, then proves in Theorem 7 that every almost connected Abelian pro-Lie group is reflexive, and only after that asks Question 3 and the stronger Question 4. This shows that the intended problem is precisely the stability of Pontryagin reflexivity under taking all subgroups and all Hausdorff quotient groups of an Abelian pro-Lie group. ([sidneymorris.net](https://www.sidneymorris.net/Morris156.pdf?utm_source=openai))
